And supporting turns by Jayne Houdyshell, Terri White, and Rosalind Elias deliver socko old-school showmanship that reminds you why, even if theaters shutter, vaudeville will never die.

With so much of the connecting tissue gone, and no visionary guide present to insist the action be a constant progression and not a journey constantly interrupted by irrelevant asides, this Follies is barely worthy of its title.
Peters and company triumph in Eric Schaeffer’s revival staging of Stephen Sondheim and James Goldman’s meditations on the follies of youth, the past and the roads not taken.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this revival of Sondheim's masterwork, praising its vibrant performances and brilliant score, though some find the production uneven. Most agree it's a worthy mounting that captures the show's emotional complexity.
